clue.text: Courage? Makes an error about one retreating

indicators.note: retreating means the whole assembly is read backwards, going back the way it came
about means the first word goes round the second piece here

parts.note: to trip is to slip up or make a mistake, so makes an error gives TRIPS
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether courage is shown by a person who blunders and then backs away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I inside TRIPS to give TIRIPS, and 'retreating' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirit is mettle or pluck, a synonym for bravery; the question mark nods to the clue's cowardly picture.

clue.text: Abandonment of rule in mine is producing chest disease

indicators.note: in means the scrambled letters go inside the other pieces

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
taken as written

indicators.note: abandonment suggests wild disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Quitting a pit's regulations leads to lung trouble among miners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandonment' reads as quitting, but in the sense of wild abandon it signals scrambling; 'in' places the jumbled letters straight after the P.
explanation.definitionFit: This is inflammation of the pleura, the membrane lining the lungs and chest cavity.

clue.text: Incompletely operate part of farm being out of practice

indicators.note: incompletely means the word for operate loses its last letter

parts.note: to run a machine is to operate it
a sty is the pigs' pen on a farm

explanation.surface: Someone half-heartedly working a section of a farm because their skills have lapsed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incompletely' cuts RUN to RU.
explanation.definitionFit: Skills that have lapsed through lack of use have deteriorated like corroded metal.

clue.text: Roman playwright in time before on one occasion expressing love

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

indicators.note: expressing in the sense of squeezing out, so the love letter is pressed out

parts.note: once means on one occasion
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A dramatist once declared his love, back in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expressing' means squeezing out, so O leaves ONCE to give NCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Terence was a comic dramatist of ancient Rome, author of six surviving comedies.

clue.text: The main section's working for run of performances

parts.note: the main is a poetic name for the open sea
S is a standard abbreviation for section
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A part of the ocean is in operation, as if the sea were a machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is old poetic language for the high sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre or opera company's season is the period during which a production runs.

clue.text: The French city near Montpellier, turning influential

indicators.note: turning means the whole thing is read backwards

parts.note: la is the French for the
Nîmes is a city close to Montpellier in southern France

explanation.surface: A French city near Montpellier becomes significant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses LANIMES.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminal work is groundbreaking, strongly affecting later developments.

clue.text: Provides kit for a cricket club, English, during various tours

indicators.note: during means the English letter comes within the mixed letters
various suggests different forms, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Outfitting a cricket club and English players for their several overseas tours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges TOURS into OUTRS, and 'during' puts E inside it before the S.
explanation.definitionFit: To accoutre is to equip or dress someone in special clothing or gear.

clue.text: One has a bad experience with daughter leaving

indicators.note: leaving means the daughter letter goes away from the word

parts.note: a downer is a depressing experience

explanation.surface: Someone suffers a miserable time when their daughter moves out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One has' looks like the start of a sentence, but it defines the answer: the one who has something.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who possesses something is its proprietor.

clue.text: Realm most disordered?

indicators.note: disordered means the letters of these two words are thrown out of their order

explanation.surface: A query about which kingdom is the most chaotic of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disordered' rearranges REALM MOST, and the whole clue also describes the answer: a scene of utter turmoil.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirlpool, figuratively any violently confused situation, is just what a realm in total disarray would be.

clue.text: Crowd surrounding university church told stories about finally giving thanks

indicators.note: surrounding means the crowd word goes round the next two letters

parts.note: a mob is a crowd

indicators.note: about means the stories word goes round that letter

parts.note: telling stories is lying, so told stories is lied

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A crowd around a college chapel told tales before saying thank you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounding' gives M-UCH-OB; 'about' gives LI-G-ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Much obliged is a polite phrase of gratitude, the same as saying thank you very much.

clue.text: Military leader around US city backing sceptical commentator

indicators.note: around means the leader's letters surround the city's

parts.note: CIC is short for commander-in-chief

indicators.note: backing means the city's letters go in backwards

parts.note: NY is New York

explanation.surface: A general supports a scornful pundit from an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns the city round before 'around' tucks it into the leader's three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who doubts people's motives and voices that doubt is a scoffer, a sceptical observer.

clue.text: Disputed promissory note stuck into early section of book?

indicators.note: stuck into means the note goes inside the book section

parts.note: the contents page comes near the front of a book
an IOU is a written promise to pay

explanation.surface: A dodgy promise to pay is found tucked into the front pages of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the contents are only one possible early section of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A contentious issue is controversial, likely to cause argument.

clue.text: Wage fuss

definitions.meaning: to wage a campaign is to carry it on, to continue it
British slang for a commotion or palaver

explanation.surface: Two bare words, pay and bother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wage' looks like a noun meaning pay, but it is the verb, as in waging war. A carry-on is a fuss in British English.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to continue doing something, like waging; the hyphenated noun means a commotion.

clue.text: Particle new to Planck, and not recalled after brief time

indicators.note: after means the following pieces come behind the brief time

parts.note: Max Planck was German, and the German for new is neu
T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so this word runs backwards

parts.note: nor means and not

explanation.surface: A physics particle unknown to Max Planck, apparently forgotten soon after.
explanation.walkthrough: Planck, the German physicist, signals a German word: NEU. 'recalled' turns NOR into RON.
explanation.definitionFit: This uncharged subatomic body sits in the atomic nucleus beside the proton.

clue.text: Dismissed article in meadow that's turned shabby

parts.note: a batter dismissed in cricket is out

indicators.note: in means the article sits inside the meadow
that's turned means the meadow word is reversed

parts.note: a lea is a poetic word for meadow
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece set in a field, rejected for having gone scruffy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's turned' reverses the meadow to AEL, and 'in' puts the article between its first letter and the rest. In cricket, a batter who is dismissed is out.
explanation.definitionFit: Out at heel describes worn, threadbare shoes and so anyone or anything shabby and down-at-heel.

clue.text: Mistake if kept in bound and frightened

indicators.note: kept in means these letters are held inside the word for bound

parts.note: something tied up is bound
to err is to make a mistake
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tied up and scared fears a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mistake' is a noun on the surface but ERR, the verb, is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrified means extremely scared, filled with terror.

clue.text: Hospital involved in remarkable cure gets decoration

indicators.note: involved in means the hospital letter goes into the reworked letters
remarkable suggests something out of the ordinary, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A hospital that took part in an amazing cure is awarded a medal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remarkable' shuffles CURE into RUCE, and 'involved in' slips H inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruche is a gathered frill of fabric used as trimming, an ornament on a garment.

clue.text: Endless sequence of ridiculous events held up navigator lacking a skilled worker

indicators.note: held up in a down entry means the letters are read from bottom to top
endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a farce is a ludicrous series of mishaps

indicators.note: lacking means the given letter is missing from the navigator's name

parts.note: Abel Tasman was the Dutch navigator who reached Tasmania and New Zealand

explanation.surface: A chain of absurd delays has kept a seafarer back, leaving him short of a deckhand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts FARCE to FARC and 'held up' reverses it to CRAF; 'lacking' takes an A from TASMAN to give TSMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan practising a trade by hand with expertise is a skilled worker.

clue.text: Beam when admitted by the French Queen

indicators.note: admitted by means the word for when is let inside the other letters

parts.note: le is the French for the
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
R, for regina, stands for queen

explanation.surface: A shaft of light shines as the French queen lets it in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' as AS is a common crossword equivalence ('as I arrived' = 'when I arrived'); 'admitted by' puts it between L and ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A laser produces a narrow, intense ray of light.

clue.text: Trouble about Director and lead actor making early beginning

indicators.note: about means the trouble word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: heat means trouble or pressure, as in 'the heat is on'
the star is the lead actor in a film

explanation.surface: A film shoot has problems involving its director and star from the very first day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble' is heat in the sense of pressure ('the heat is on'); 'about' wraps it round the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A head start is an advantage given at the outset of a race, starting ahead of rivals.

clue.text: Accepting defeat, mostly recover, taking devious course?

indicators.note: accepting means the word for recover takes the other letters inside

parts.note: to heal is to recover

indicators.note: mostly means the word for defeat loses its last letter

parts.note: to lick an opponent is to defeat them

explanation.surface: Taking a beating and partly getting better, someone goes about things in a roundabout way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the final K, and 'Accepting' takes the result inside. The question mark admits that a spiral path is only playfully 'devious'.
explanation.definitionFit: A helix winds round and round, so a spiral route is a winding, indirect path.

clue.text: A rumour about ready money getting 17?

definitions.note: the answer to 17 across is an example of the kind of word wanted

indicators.note: about means the rumour word surrounds the ready word

parts.note: a cry can be a report or rumour going round
on means ready or prepared, as in 'game on'

explanation.surface: A rumour concerning cash is going round in the run-up to something.
explanation.walkthrough: '17?' refers to the answer at 17 across, a word built from initials (Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation); the question mark marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A word formed from the initial letters of a phrase, pronounced as a word, is the type the beam word belongs to.

clue.text: Good lines about active spies being very reserved

indicators.note: about means the two line letters enclose the others

parts.note: L is short for line, so lines are LL
the CIA is the US spy agency

explanation.surface: Fine words about working secret agents who keep themselves to themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A + CIA between the two Ls.
explanation.definitionFit: Icily cold in manner, as unfriendly and distant as a glacier, is extremely reserved.

clue.text: Chance to forgo start of gruelling walk

indicators.note: to forgo means the word for chance does without that letter

parts.note: a gamble is a chance or risk

indicators.note: start of means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An opportunity to skip the opening of an exhausting hike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to forgo' drops the G given by 'start of gruelling'.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to stroll at a leisurely pace.

clue.text: Set up H2O around rear of chalet? Absolutely

parts.note: to rig something is to set it up, as a rig a stage

indicators.note: around means the formula's letters surround the chalet's last letter

parts.note: the formula is read letter by letter, two Hs and an O

indicators.note: rear of means the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Plumbing water round the back of a ski chalet, with eager agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: H2O is taken literally as H, H, O, and 'around' places T between the Hs and the O.
explanation.definitionFit: Right-ho is an old-fashioned British exclamation of agreement, much like saying certainly or of course.

clue.text: "Boring thing" (dismissing male jacket)

indicators.note: dismissing means the male letter is sent out of the tool's name

parts.note: a gimlet is a small hand tool for boring holes

explanation.surface: A dull item of clothing gets rid of the man wearing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring thing' reads as dull, but it is a tool that bores holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A gilet is a sleeveless padded jacket or waistcoat.

clue.text: Name given to excellent city

indicators.note: given to means the second piece is attached to the first

parts.note: to dub is to name, as in a knight
A1 (written AI) means first-rate

explanation.surface: A name is bestowed on a splendid metropolis.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, first-rate, is read with the 1 as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubai is the glittering Gulf metropolis in the United Arab Emirates.

clue.text: Arranged slam-dance festival

indicators.note: arranged means these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A festival is organised around a mosh-pit style of dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arranged' rearranges the letters of SLAM-DANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Candlemas, on 2 February, is the Christian feast of the Presentation of Christ, marked with blessed candles.

clue.text: Like a social structure expected to return in autumn? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means the assembly loses its final letter
in means the reversed word goes inside the season

parts.note: fall is the American word for autumn

indicators.note: to return means the word for expected goes in backwards

parts.note: due means expected, as a train due at noon

explanation.surface: Some social order is predicted to come back in autumn, but only partly.
explanation.walkthrough: Autumn is the American fall. 'to return' reverses the word for expected to EUD, 'in' puts it inside, giving FEUDALL, and 'Not entirely' drops the last L.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval system of lords, vassals and fiefs was a hierarchy of land tenure, a kind of social structure.

clue.text: Finishing game, ready to get engrossed in periodical

indicators.note: to get engrossed in means the money word is buried within the periodical

parts.note: a mag is a magazine, a periodical
the ready is slang for cash, as is tin

explanation.surface: A finished match, and someone settling in with a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' and 'tin' are both old British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess, checkmating the opposing king is what ends the game.
